newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Armed robbers prey on Nigerian fair exhibitors.
newsitem.headline: Armed robbers prey on Nigerian fair exhibitors.

text.p: Fifteen armed robbers attacked trade fair exhibitors in their hotel in the northern Nigerian city of Kaduna, stealing cash and property worth five million naira ($58,823), local newspapers reported on Saturday.
They said robbers stormed the hotel on Friday night and went from room to room robbing and beating up guests, most of them Nigerians attending an African trade fair in the city.

"They knocked on my door and when I asked who was there, they replied that they were armed robbers and ordered me to open the door," Salihu Ndangi, a senior official of R.T. Briscoe Company, told the independent Guardian newspaper.

"I opened it and at gun-point, they collected 16,700 naira plus two wrist watches, one scientific calculator, a cap worth 1,500 naira and two bags which they used in carting away their loot," he added.

The paper said items lost to the robbers included jewelry, electronic equipment, shoes and bags meant for exhibition at the fair while guests at the hotel who did not have much money or valuable items for the robbers to steal were beaten up.
Although armed robbery is punishable by death by firing squad in Nigeria, it is on the increase because of economic hardship in Africa's most populous nation.
